newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Guests leap from burning Philippine hotel, 8 die.
newsitem.headline: Guests leap from burning Philippine hotel, 8 die.

text.p: Eight people died and more than 20 were injured when a fire raged through a hotel in the southern Philippines early on Saturday, forcing some guests to jump from their windows, police said.
Investigators said firemen battled their way through heavy smoke to search gutted rooms of the popular six-storey Imperial Hotel in Cotabato city. The death toll could rise, they said.
It was the worst fire to occur in the country since 152 people, mostly teenagers, were killed in a disco fire in Manila on March 19 last year.
The injured included hotel guests who broke their legs after leaping through their windows, some wearing only their underwear, in order to escape, witnesses said.
"I jumped like Superman. Now, you see my legs are broken," hotel guest Nur Baiman told Reuters while undergoing treatment at a local hospital.

Saudi Arabian preacher Al Daruis, who suffered bruises, said he escaped by wrapping himself up with a water-soaked blanket and running down a burning hallway on the third floor of the hotel in the city centre.
"I was fortunate because I was awake...I was praying," Daruis said. "I smelt smoke and when I opened the door the hallway was full of smoke...I called downstairs and people said there was a fire."
He then grabbed his blanket and drenched it in water.
"I was asleep in my room when I woke up feeling as if I was choking. It was the smoke," said guest Jimmy Malcampo, who survived with leg injuries after leaping through a third floor window.
"I rushed out of my room and saw the hall on fire. My choice was to die or jump out of the window. I jumped," he said.
Another guest, Roger Araila, said he was wearing only his briefs when he jumped through the window of his third floor room, also breaking his legs.
Some survived by climbing down firemen's ladders.
Chief arson investigator Abdulazak Mosa said five of the eight fatalities suffocated after being trapped in their rooms or in hallways while trying to flee. Two of the dead were women.
"We have not determined whether the fire was accidental or intentional. We are still investigating," he said.
Initial probes showed the fire, which gutted three floors of the building, broke out in a prayer room used by both Moslems and Christians.
Only a few dozen guests were at the hotel when the blaze started at 12.30 a.m.
"It could have been worse if the fire happened later because we were expecting foreign dignitaries," a hotel official said.

The foreign officials were to hear a state-of-the-region address by former Moslem rebel chief Nur Misuari, who now runs a four-province Moslem autonomous region on the southern island of Mindanao after signing a peace pact with Manila last year.
Misuari has his headquarters in Cotabato, a predominantly Moslem city 900 kms (560 miles) south of Manila.
